status_summary: No action found eliminates the Impact Aid payments not tied to students or moves student-driven Impact Aid to the Defense Department's schools or the Bureau of Indian Education. Under an interagency agreement signed on 2025-09-30, the Department of Labor's Employment and Training Administration provides services supporting the administration of Impact Aid, including Section 7002 Payments for Federal Property, under Department of Education supervision. The Department's FY2027 request funds all five Impact Aid lines, with Payments for Federal Property at $80 million against $79 million in FY2025. A bill introduced on 2026-07-09 (H.R. 9610) would transfer Impact Aid functions to the Secretary of Labor, a destination different from the one in the text.

timeline.event: The Departments of Education and Labor signed the Elementary and Secondary Education Partnership interagency agreement; item 31 has Labor provide services supporting the administration of Impact Aid sections 7002, 7003, 7007(b) and 7008, in coordination with and under the supervision of the Department of Education.

The Department of Education announced six interagency partnerships, including an elementary and secondary education partnership under which Labor takes a greater role in administering federal K-12 programs.

The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (Public Law 119-75) was approved; Division B is the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education appropriations act for FY2026, which funds Impact Aid.

The FY2027 President's budget request for the Department of Education funds all five Impact Aid lines, including $80 million for Payments for Federal Property (Section 7002), for a total of about $1.63 billion. (month only; first of month used)
H.R. 9610 (Less Bureaucracy, Better K-12 Education Act) was introduced; section 2 would transfer Impact Aid under ESEA title VII from the Secretary of Education to the Secretary of Labor.

title: Eliminate Impact Aid not tied to students; move student-driven Impact Aid to DoDEA or BIE
uncertainties: The FY2027 release date is given as April 2026; a law-firm summary gives 2026-04-03, which the Department tables do not print. The FY2026 request (congressional justification on ed.gov) failed to load for both the researcher and the reviewer. An association of federally impacted schools reported a $5 million increase for Impact Aid in the FY2026 law, House committee approval of H.R. 9610 in July 2026, and a Senate committee vote on S. 5046, which would bar the transfer; none was confirmed from a primary source, and the Impact Aid figures in Division B of Public Law 119-75 were not read because the GovInfo page was truncated. The interagency agreement describes Labor as providing administrative services under Department of Education supervision rather than taking over the program; whether that counts as a move is a matter of degree. Searches run: ed.gov and nafisdc.org terms on Impact Aid budget requests, interagency agreements and appropriations (researcher); ed.gov and dol.gov terms on the interagency agreement text and Impact Aid (reviewer, three searches). No transfer to DoDEA or BIE was found. Indian education transfers to Interior are tracked in c11-02.
